summary.headline: Navin Fluorine Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 57% YoY to INR1,191 crores, with EBITDA margin at 34.2%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 operating revenue was INR1,191 crores (+57% YoY), operating EBITDA INR407 crores (+66%) at a 34.2% margin, and PAT INR269 crores (+81%). H1 FY27 revenue reached INR2,236 crores (+51%), EBITDA INR765 crores (+69%, margin up 367 bps to 34.2%) and PAT INR513 crores (+93%), with EPS of INR100. Management attributed growth to ref gas pricing, AHF volumes, the Solstice HFO contract, specialty campaigns and CDMO qualifications. The HFO contract with Solstice was extended to December 2032 with about USD180 million of additional revenue potential, though the implied annual run rate is lower than the prior one, which management attributed to pricing mechanics.

financial_highlights.change: +93% YoY vs INR320 crores in H1 FY26

segments.name: HPP (Hydrofluoropolymers / ref gases, AHF, HFO)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew sequentially on better realisations in ref gas and higher AHF volumes after the new AHF plant came into play; HFC realisations improved QoQ. The Solstice HFO contract extension runs to December 2032, with about USD180 million of added revenue potential over four years.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Run rate has been stated at about INR350 crores for the last three quarters. MPP-1 and MPP-2 are expected to far exceed PAR by end FY27; the MPP debottlenecking at Dahej was commissioned in September 2026. Nectar is expected at 60-65% of PAR in FY27, with the balance in FY28.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Management says the USD100 million order-book visibility target is within striking distance and is on time for FY27. The cGMP-4 Phase 2 capex of about INR125 crores is due by end Q4 FY27 and is fully dedicated to Fermion. Phase 1 plus Phase 2 is guided to a peak annual revenue potential of INR900-1,000 crores by FY28-FY29.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to stay in the range of the H1 FY27 level of about 34%; the 30% long-term guidance was not changed.
Capex frame of INR700-1,000 crores a year; FY27 is tracking to the lower end at about INR700 crores.
R32 capacity expected to commission shortly, with incremental growth this quarter and full ramp-up in the next quarter.
Chemours advanced cooling project expected to commission in Q3 FY27; about 15 months after commissioning is needed to gauge adoption and final capex.
Advanced Materials expected to contribute about 10-15% of the expanded revenue pie by 2030, under a 20-25% growth frame.
Advanced material adoption capacity expected to commission by Q2 FY28; HFC capacity expansion on track for commissioning shortly.
capex_capacity: Debottlenecking of MPP capacity at Dahej commissioned in September 2026; growth from it is not yet in the numbers.
HFC capacity expansion progressing as planned; R32 capex on track for commissioning shortly.
Chemours project progressing towards commissioning in Q3 FY27; purchase orders already in hand.
cGMP-4 Phase 2 (about INR125 crores) to be operational by end Q4 FY27; ETP and warehouse infrastructure exist for up to Phase 5/6, so cGMP-5 could follow quickly.
TDF project with DRDO progressing per schedule; renewable energy investments expected to cover more than 60% of energy requirements.
demand_pricing: Ref gas pricing improved on a sequential basis; management says teams placed product above the market average.
HF merchant sales are running well above the earlier plan, with some material going to international markets and high-purity HF.
Cost pressures are visible in sulfur, gas and fluorspar; management says the 34% margin cannot come from pricing alone and relies on efficiency gains and forex tailwinds.
HFO demand is expected to rise with construction and chiller applications; the Solstice contract volumes are based on minimum customer quantities.
Specialty order visibility is strong for H2 FY27 and beyond; five new molecules have campaign orders running to end-FY27 and beyond.
Management said global HFO capacity is about 10% of global ref gas demand in tonnage, so HFO is priced at a premium to ref gases.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the QoQ growth across all three segments, and what drives growth from the Q2 base?
qa_highlights.answer: HPP grew on better ref gas pricing and AHF volumes, with QoQ growth also from the Solstice HFO business. Specialty gained from campaign efficiency in MPP plants, and CDMO from Fermion and new qualifications. Future growth comes from Dahej debottlenecking, R32 ramp-up and CDMO scale-up.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the Solstice extension imply a lower annual run rate (about USD45 million versus about USD58 million)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the contract is a pass-through pricing mechanism, so a simple average is misleading. It extends the same asset base to an 11-year contract from 7 years, with larger expected volumes; the pricing can change once capex is recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Will HFO commercialisation be delayed by supplying Honeywell beyond 2030?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said there are about 40 HFO varieties, and products outside the conflicting application can be pursued through partnership or product models.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Chemours commissioning delay affecting qualification?
qa_highlights.answer: The delay was a deliberate choice to pick the right process route for the initial capacity, not a partner-side issue. Orders are already in place for future quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CDMO target beyond USD100 million and what are the timelines for cGMP-5?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 and Phase 2 together have a peak revenue potential of about 3x capex, or INR900-1,000 crores by FY28-FY29. cGMP-5 would be triggered when GMP utilisation reaches 70-80%, and one molecule has approval in China and is on a fast track for FDA approval.

qa_highlights.question: How should capex and surplus cash be allocated?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex frame is INR700-1,000 crores a year, with FY27 at about INR700 crores and the lower end of the range. Working capital is held at 70-75 days, EBITDA conversion is 60-65%, and new capex will be announced after stage-gate approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Chemours 10x scale-up trigger and the OEM adoption signal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is premature to size the final capex, which will be clearer after about 15 months of adoption data post-commissioning. Chemours has qualified with a French OEM, 2CRSi, under a joint development agreement, and purchase orders are in hand.

risks_watch: Solstice HFO contract run rate of about USD45 million a year versus about USD58 million previously; the pricing mechanism and post-patent HFO price erosion remain unclear.
Input cost inflation (sulfur, gas, fluorspar, HF) and geopolitical volatility, which management says are not over.
Chemours project commissioning in Q3 FY27 and the roughly 15-month adoption window before final capex is known.
AHF plant utilisation is still ramping and management declined to give a utilisation figure.
Whether the 34% margin holds in FY27 and whether the 30% long-term margin guidance is revisited.
Specialty run rate of INR350 crores versus the Dahej debottlenecking benefit that is not yet in the numbers; R32 full ramp-up expected in the next quarter.
Management declined to discuss the DRDO economics beyond schedule and the dual-use pharma route.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and execution, with specific timelines for commissioning. Guarded and evasive on forward margins, the HFO pricing post-patent, and AHF utilisation, where management repeatedly said averages are misleading and declined to give numbers.

I will not sit here and let you believe that I have full knowledge of the future.
